name: netdiag
description: Read-only network troubleshooting from wherever Loyd runs: ping, trace, DNS, ports, HTTP/TLS, interfaces, neighbours, listening sockets, and a layered outage check.

commands.name: triage
commands.description: Something's out? Checks this device, the gateway, DNS, the internet, then optionally one service, and stops at the first layer that fails, saying which.

service.description: optional hostname to check last, e.g. hihilabs.xyz

commands.run:
gw=$(ip route 2>/dev/null | awk '/^default/ {print $3; exit}')
echo "1 this device: $(hostname), gateway ${gw:-none}"
[ -n "$gw" ] || { echo "STOP at 1: no default route. Check Wi-Fi or cable."; exit 1; }
if ping -c 2 -W 2 "$gw" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "2 gateway $gw: answering"; else echo "STOP at 2: gateway $gw not answering. Router or local link is down."; exit 1; fi
if getent hosts one.one.one.one >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "3 DNS via $(awk '/^nameserver/ {print $2; exit}' /etc/resolv.conf): resolving"; else
  if dig @1.1.1.1 +short +time=2 +tries=1 one.one.one.one 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then echo "STOP at 3: local DNS server is failing, but the internet works (1.1.1.1 answers)."; else echo "STOP at 3: DNS failing, and 1.1.1.1 does not answer either. Internet is probably down."; fi; exit 1; fi
if ping -c 2 -W 3 1.1.1.1 >/dev/null 2>&1 || curl -sS -m 6 -o /dev/null https://1.1.1.1 2>/dev/null; then echo "4 internet: reachable"; else echo "STOP at 4: no route to the internet (gateway and DNS fine). ISP or upstream outage."; exit 1; fi
svc={service}
if [ -n "$svc" ]; then
  ip=$(getent hosts "$svc" | awk '{print $1; exit}')
  case "$ip" in 10.*|192.168.*|172.1[6-9].*|172.2[0-9].*|172.3[01].*|100.*) where=LAN/tailnet;; "") where=unresolved;; *) where=public;; esac
  code=$(curl -sS -m 8 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$svc" 2>/dev/null)
  echo "5 $svc: resolves to ${ip:-nothing} ($where), HTTPS status ${code:-no answer}"
fi
echo "OK: every layer checked is up."

commands.name: ping
commands.description: Ping a host a few times (packet loss and round-trip time).

commands.name: trace
commands.description: Trace the route to a host, one probe per hop, numeric addresses.

commands.name: dns_lookup
commands.description: Look up a DNS record through this device's resolver.

commands.name: dns_compare
commands.description: Resolve a name through the local resolver and through 1.1.1.1 side by side; a difference means split DNS (or a local DNS problem).

commands.name: port
commands.description: Test whether a TCP port accepts connections, with connect time.

commands.name: http
commands.description: Fetch a URL's status, total time and the IP it connected to (no body).

commands.name: tls_cert
commands.description: Who a TLS certificate is for, who issued it, and when it expires.

commands.name: interfaces
commands.description: This device's addresses, routes and DNS servers.
commands.run: ip -brief addr; echo; ip route; echo; grep -v '^#' /etc/resolv.conf

commands.name: neighbors
commands.description: Devices this machine has recently talked to on the local network (IP and MAC).

commands.name: listening
commands.description: Ports this machine is listening on, and which program holds each.
